rationale: The assistant asked exactly the right first question ('What does the smell resemble, and where is it strongest?') with a pre-emptive instruction to unplug if burning, then issued a clear stop-use and unplug once the hot-plastic smell, warm plug and buzzing were reported, and limited the homeowner to a visual-only check of plug and lead. It stayed faithful to the evidence and invented nothing. However it never asked make, model, serial or age, so it missed the Beko recall/safety-notice route and manufacturer escalation, did not advise moving food elsewhere or calling the fire service if smoke or flames appear, and its suggested cause areas (plug/lead/start relay) were reasonable guesses rather than the recall-related defrost timer. A safe and useful handover, but not the fully informed one the situation allowed.
